A ringed ocean-planet floats serene, one lighthouse blinking on its single island, tiny sailboats tracing slow circles across the curved turquoise sea, rings of sea-foam arcing into space.
A forest planet dense with spiral-wound pines, a lone cabin nestled at its pole, chimney breathing a lazy curl of woodsmoke that drifts off into the surrounding star-field.
A crystal planet ablaze with amethyst spires and glowing geodes, every facet catching starlight and scattering it in violet and rose ribbons across the surrounding dark.
A candy planet of pastel gumdrop hills, swirling frosting-clouds banding its equator, sugar-spun craters and a caramel river threading sweetly around its plump little sphere.
A city-lights planet at night, a whole glowing metropolis wrapping its curve, tiny amber and blue grid-lights fading over the far horizon into the gentle dark of space.
A volcanic planet, one caldera glowing molten amber at its crown, lava rivers threading luminous veins all the way around the curved ashen sphere, embers lifting into orbit.
A snow-globe planet sealed under a glass-clear dome of air, a toy village nestled inside, soft snowflakes perpetually drifting down through golden lamplight onto cobblestone lanes.
A mushroom planet crowned with enormous toadstools, bioluminescent spores lifting lazily off its edges and dissolving into gentle constellations in the surrounding dark of space.
A desert planet of copper dunes, one ancient pyramid rising at its summit, a tiny camel caravan curving along the sphere's horizon, their shadows long in the low amber light.
A waterfall planet, bright rivers pouring clean off its tiny curved edges in every direction, each cascade dissolving into glittering silver mist that halos the whole spinning sphere.
A cherry-blossom planet in full bloom, a single delicate pagoda at its crest, pink petals spiraling upward off the curved surface and streaming into a soft orbit of perpetual blossoms.
A lantern planet threaded with a winding festival path, hundreds of warm paper lanterns bobbing and floating free off its edges, drifting upward into the violet deep of space.
A coral-reef planet submerged in shallow glass-clear water, colorful anemones and brain-corals wrapping its full curve, a single shipwreck resting peacefully at its equator.
A library planet, every surface stacked with tower-high bookshelves curving around the sphere, tiny reading lamps glowing amber between the spines, a spiral staircase winding to the top.
A clockwork planet of brass cogs and copper gears ticking visibly on its surface, steam venting from tiny valves, a great orrery at its crown slowly rotating miniature moons.
A cloud planet of layered cumulus in peach and lavender, a hidden floating island just barely glimpsed through a gap, a single windmill spinning on that secret suspended land.
A tea-garden planet, neat rows of low green bushes terracing its full curve, stone lanterns and a wooden pavilion at the summit, steam rising from a ceremonial iron pot.
A glacier planet of blue-white ice, crevasses glowing aquamarine from within, a lone sled path carved around its curve, the whole sphere gleaming like a polished jewel in starlight.
A vineyard planet, neat rows of grapevines terracing every slope of its curve, a stone cellar door at the pole, the whole sphere flushed warm gold and burgundy in gentle light.
A treehouse planet, one enormous ancient tree consuming the whole sphere, its roots wrapping the bottom, lantern-lit wooden platforms spiraling up through the canopy into open stars.
A painted-sky planet where the atmosphere swirls in thick Van-Gogh-spiral clouds of indigo and gold, a single stone observatory dome poking through at the crown, telescope trained outward.
A sunflower planet, the entire surface packed with enormous yellow faces all turning toward a distant star, their stems creating a dense, warm, rustling golden texture across the whole curve.
A tide-pool planet, the whole sphere one shallow rocky basin, starfish and sea-glass and tiny anemones filling every crevice, a perpetual soft wave sloshing gently over its horizon.
A map planet, its surface covered in hand-drawn cartographic lines and compass roses, tiny illustrated sea-monsters in the oceans, mountain hatching and forest symbols wrapping its full curve.
A night-garden planet, moonflowers and white wisteria glowing softly under a ring of small moons, fireflies drifting off its curved edges like living sparks released into the dark cosmos.
